headline: High: next-ai-draw-io can exfiltrate via broad egress while taipy is local-only, creating asymmetric leakage and workflow-conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io ingests PDFs, text, images, and draw.io XML and uses MCP/browser tooling, so attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. taipy has no documented input isolation or provenance controls, so if its outputs are fed into next-ai-draw-io, prompt injection is plausible. The shared path is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF taipy outputs are copied into next-ai-draw-io without sanitization, injection risk is present.
IF next-ai-draw-io parses file content as instructions, malicious document text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted documents.
Add a manual review step before passing taipy outputs onward.
Strip instruction-like text from imported files.
Use a provenance tag on all transferred artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and trust boundaries in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress and can call multiple third-party model APIs while handling PDFs, text, images, and diagrams; taipy is documented as network-egress none. If sensitive files flow from taipy into next-ai-draw-io, the pair can leak data to external inference providers. The interaction is inferred from profiles, but the exfiltration path is explicit on agent_a.
conditions: IF taipy-managed data is forwarded into next-ai-draw-io, external API transmission can occur.
IF next-ai-draw-io is configured to use OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar APIs, file contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep sensitive taipy datasets out of next-ai-draw-io.
Select a local-only model backend for next-ai-draw-io.
Redact secrets before import.
Review outbound API settings before each run.
requires-engineering: add egress allowlisting and DLP controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances and broad network egress, but taipy exposes no write surfaces or shared mutable resources in the profile. There is no documented overlapping filesystem, git, or database write target, so a direct capability conflict is not evidenced. Uncertainty remains because taipy's write surfaces are unspecified, so the safer low severity is chosen.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or database, write conflicts can occur.
IF taipy is configured with mutable shared state, concurrent updates may race.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared artifacts.
Serialize edits through one operator.
Check for hidden shared mounts before launch.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io performs AI-assisted visualization and natural-language commands, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream automation. taipy is a data-engineering and job-scheduler tool, which makes it plausible that taipy consumes or acts on those outputs. Because no verification or guardrail is documented, a mistaken diagram or instruction can cascade into incorrect actions.
conditions: IF taipy consumes next-ai-draw-io-generated instructions or diagrams without validation, errors can propagate.
IF next-ai-draw-io output is used as a source of truth, downstream automation may act on incorrect content.
mitigations: Require human approval before execution.
Compare outputs against source documents.
Use checksum or schema validation on transferred artifacts.
Limit taipy to read-only consumption of diagrams.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: next-ai-draw-io explicitly handles API keys and can send content to third-party model providers, while taipy documents no data classes or residency controls. If regulated or sensitive data from taipy is processed by next-ai-draw-io, retention and residency obligations may be violated. The compliance risk is one-sided because taipy itself shows no outbound handling, but the pair still creates a mismatch.
conditions: IF taipy data includes regulated records and is sent to next-ai-draw-io, residency or retention obligations may be breached.
IF next-ai-draw-io uses third-party APIs with different retention terms, compliance mismatch arises.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workflow.
Confirm vendor retention settings for each API backend.
Document a data-handling policy for imported files.
Purge temporary artifacts after each run.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and retention controls.
